get.summary: What a client needs to know before anyone signs in.
get.description:
What a client needs to know before anyone signs in.
 The website reads these from its own build (NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables), which a mobile app cannot see. Without this it would have to hard-code them: whether payments run through M-Pesa Daraja or a manual till, whether M-Pesa is the sandbox (where a "simulate" shortcut is offered) or live, the numbers to call in an emergency, and the rules a password or an upload must satisfy. Serving them from the API means a change here reaches every client without a release.
 Public by design and contains nothing secret.

post.summary: Legacy direct-Daraja webhook, kept for environments running PAYMENTS_MODE=mpesa_daraja without Jenga creden…
post.description: Legacy direct-Daraja webhook, kept for environments running PAYMENTS_MODE=mpesa_daraja without Jenga credentials yet. Matches by gatewayRef (Daraja's CheckoutRequestID) against the polymorphic Payment table — one lookup now covers appointments, orders, and home visits. Daraja expects a 200 with { ResultCode: 0, ResultDesc: "Success" }.

post.summary: Dev/sandbox helper.
post.description: Dev/sandbox helper. Sandbox gateways (Daraja and Jenga UAT alike) don't reliably post a real success callback, so this fires the same success outcome our webhooks handle, completing the matching appointment payment, pharmacy order, or home-visit payment. Gated on NODE_ENV, not just MPESA_ENV — a production deploy that forgets to set MPESA_ENV must not leave this reachable.

get.summary: A verified provider's public photo as a real image.
get.description:
A verified provider's public photo as a real image.
 Photos are stored as base64 data: URLs in the database. Putting those straight into pages meant every provider list shipped megabytes of text inside the HTML and could not be cached or indexed as an image. Serving them from a URL fixes all three. The URL carries a version (`?v=`) that changes with the photo, so it can be cached for a year without anyone seeing a stale picture.
 Only verified providers' photos are served. A patient's avatar is not public.
